items.title: Karnataka to regulate hospital bills, frame policy against withholding bodies over dues
items.summary: The Karnataka government will introduce measures to curb excessive hospital billing, regulate medicine mark-ups and improve transparency in treatment costs, Health Minister UT Khader said on Thursday, October 22. The state will also formulate a policy to prevent hospitals from withholding deceased patients’ bodies over unpaid medical bills. Speaking after a meeting with representatives of the Private Hospitals and Nursing Homes Association (PHANA) in Bengaluru, Khader said hospitals would have to display the rates of major medical procedures at their reception counters from November 1. They would also be required to maintain a register listing the prices of other procedures, given that hospitals offer more than 4,000 types of medical procedures. “There are over 4,000 medical procedures offered by hospitals and it is not possible to display all the prices. Hence, we have directed them to put up large, readable boards listing the rates of important procedures and maintain a register with the prices of other procedures,” he said. items.title: Public trustee regime and Tata Trusts: An old law, a contemporary question
items.summary: When charitable trusts control a substantial stake in a major commercial enterprise, who should determine how that voting power is exercised? The question has acquired renewed significance in the dispute over Tata Sons’ proposed listing, where disagreements within the Tata Trusts have brought fiduciary obligations, boardroom independence and corporate control into sharp focus. India once addressed a related concern through the erstwhile Section 187B of the Companies Act, 1956 (the “1956 Act”), which has since been replaced by the Companies Act, 2013 (the “2013 Act”). Inserted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 1963 with effect from January 1, 1964, the provision transferred voting rights attached to certain trust-held shares from trustees to a government-appointed Public Trustee. It sought to prevent voting power held through trusts from advancing private interests but did so without requiring an individual finding of misconduct. Parliament discontinued the regime in 2000, the same year Tata Sons, whose controlling shareholding has long been held by charitable trusts, amended its Articles of Association to give those trusts board-level rights. items.title: Bombay High Court quashes FIR against Pune college principal, teachers over Murud beach tragedy
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has quashed a 2016 FIR registered against the trustees, principal and faculty members of a Pune college over the drowning of 14 students at Murud beach in Raigad [PA Inamdar & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Anr.] The Court held that unlike minors requiring strict care, mature students understand consequences and hence, college teachers cannot be held vicariously liable under Section 304A (causing death by negligence) of Indian Penal Code (IPC) for seaside mishaps. In an order passed on October 22, the Court also directed the Maharashtra government to formulate a comprehensive beach safety policy. “If safety measures are employed as suggested above, it will not lead to a loss of human life as visitors will exercise a greater degree of caution while venturing into the sea water,” Justice Milind N Jadhav observed. Justice Milind Jadhav Therefore, the Court directed the State Tourism Ministry to draft a blueprint for crowded beaches, install bilingual warnings in English and Marathi displaying high tide timings, and deploy lifeguards and watchtowers to avert future tragedies. items.title: Parents or police can't force adult woman to return home against her wishes: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has observed that an adult woman cannot be compelled to return to her parental home against her wishes by the police or her parents on a missing person complaint. [XXX v State of Kerala & ors] Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas made the observation while disposing of a petition filed by a 22-year-old woman who alleged that police were repeatedly summoning her to the police station after she left her family home to pursue her education. In a judgment delivered on September 26, the judge said that a woman above the age of 18 has the right to make her own decisions, including where she wishes to decide. " Notwithstanding the above, since the petitioner asserts that she is now residing at Thrissur and does not intend to go back to her parental home, she, being a major, is entitled to take decisions about her. Neither her parents nor the police can interfere with such freedom to decide, " the judge said. items.title: Nothing wrong in call for regime change: Neha Bora to Delhi High Court in SEM notice case
items.summary: All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora told the Delhi High Court on Thursday that in a democracy, there is nothing wrong in making a call for a regime change. Bora was responding to the argument by Delhi Police that they (Bora has been referred to by they/ them pronouns) were part of the gathering in which a call was made for change of regime. "Joint sitting with CJP leaders and Prashant Bhushan where it was said ye regime change ki ladai hai aur ham regime change karwa ke rahenge. She was part of the same gathering," the law officer for Delhi Police contended. "There is nothing wrong with regime change in a democracy," Bora's counsel said. "Do we need to go into that?" the Court asked. "Regime change will (have to) happen by votes, not by lumpen elements congregating in New Delhi," the Delhi Police replied. The Court was hearing a plea filed by Bora challenging a notice issued to them by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) directing them to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 and maintain peace.
